main_body: Flat-roofed desert building: a large sand-coloured terrace roof with a teal dome on top, over a brick front wall with an arched door and a small barred window
top_band: Sand roof surface, L≈190 (#e3b77e) with lighter #f2d3a0 speckles, rows 3-33 at x=32. A lighter front-edge lip sits at rows 30-33. It is separated from the brick face (L≈108-137) by the dark row 34.
evidence: The column at x=32 reads as a light roof surface with a dome (rows 3-33), then a lip highlight (rows 30-33), then a dark eave row (34-36), then a brick wall (rows 37-65) with its own shading. The roof is a clearly visible horizontal surface with a parapet rim, so it is not a flat band hat. The top is quite tall and weakly foreshortened, but it clearly reads as a terrace roof seen from above. The door has a pale frame and darker panels, and the window has a sill, which gives a modest sense of inset. Both major parts, roof and wall, satisfy the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The outlines are tinted dark brown (0% neutral dark edge pixels), so they are not sticker-like, and flat-fill coverage is only 1%. The sand speckle and the teal dome are reasonably shaded. The piece is still clearly thinner than the references. It has only 30 distinct colours against 66 and 185, and a median of 8 colours per tile against 11 and 18. The brick wall uses about 3 tones with repeated, uniform bricks, and the sand roof is mostly one tone with scattered dots. That gives about 4 steps per material against the references' 5-6, with less per-element shading than the tile and stone references. It would look flatter and simpler beside them.
